Below is the one-line patch that prevents the F# “multiply-as-function” form `(*)` from being eaten as a comment opener. We simply add a negative lookahead so that `(*` immediately followed by `)` is not treated as the start of a comment.

```javascript
### components/prism-fsharp.js

            pattern: /(^|[^\\])\(\*[\s\S]*?\*\)/,
            lookbehind: true
        },
=======
        {
            // do not treat the operator form (*) as a comment
            pattern: /(^|[^\\])\(\*(?!\))[\s\S]*?\*\)/,
            lookbehind: true
        },
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```

Explanation
1. The original regex `/\(\*[\s\S]*?\*\)/` will match any `(* … *)`, including the standalone operator form `(*)`.  
2. By adding the negative lookahead `(?!\))` right after `\(\*`, we ensure that `(*` followed immediately by `)` does not count as the start of a comment.  
3. Everything else (true multiline comments) is still matched normally.

Below is a quick summary of what’s happening, the root cause, and a single one-line change you need to make in `components/prism-fsharp.js` to stop `( * )`–style operator sections from being eaten by your comment regexp.

1. Bug scenario  
   In F# you often turn the “multiply” operator into a function by writing `( * )`. Prism’s existing comment regex sees any `( *…* )` pair and assumes it’s a `(* … *)` comment, so your entire function–call gets highlighted as a comment:

     Screenshot (from your example):

       let countScore cat = … |> (*) (int cat)

     Prism highlights from the first `(*)` all the way down to the matching `*)`.

2. Root cause  
   The comment-pattern in `prism-fsharp.js` is simply

       /(^|[^\\])\(\*[\s\S]*?\*\)/

   which will happily match an empty comment `(*)` (and swallow your operator). We need to tell it NOT to match when the very next character after `(*` is `)`.

3. Fix  
   Change that regexp to `/\(\*(?!\))[\s\S]*?\*\)/` (i.e. “match `(* … *)` only if the `*` is not immediately followed by `)`) and keep the lookbehind.

Here’s the minimal *SEARCH/REPLACE* patch:

```javascript
### components/prism-fsharp.js
<<<<<<< SEARCH
    'comment': [
        {
            pattern: /(^|[^\\])\(\*[\s\S]*?\*\)/,
            lookbehind: true
        },
=======
    'comment': [
        {
            // do not treat "(*)" (the multiply-operator form) as a comment
            pattern: /(^|[^\\])\(\*(?!\))[\s\S]*?\*\)/,
            lookbehind: true
        },
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```

After you apply that, `( * )` will be left alone (and fall through to your operator grammar) while real `(* … *)` blocks still get highlighted as comments.
